body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{global,reg}}\), there is a coupling with \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\) such that \[\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\left|\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n-b_{n,k}\}-G_{n,k}\right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1),\quad \max_{k,l\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat\Gamma_n(k,l)-\Gamma_n(k,l)|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1),\] and \[\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat C_{n,k}/n-\mathfrak r_{n,k}|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1).\] Uniformly over the local subclass \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), the sharper boundary coupling \[\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\] also holds. The first display specializes at any deterministic prefix to Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's fixed-set expansion, while the suprema cover their generated all-top-\(k\) path.
body.justification: This closes the invalid pointwise-to-random-prefix step and exposes the non-Gaussian quadratic noise in the estimated MSE under local misspecification.
body.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's Theorem~2 is pointwise for a given borrowed set, while their Theorem~3 applies that control to the data-dependent minimizer without a uniform generated-ranking argument.
body.consumer: Analysts using the released influence-borrowing implementation obtain a justified joint covariance object for every candidate prefix and for the selected ATE.
